2025/26.theme: Bottom-Up Economic Transformation Agenda (BETA) for Inclusive Growth, Job Creation, and Poverty Reduction
2025/26.synopsis: Parliament approved a KES 4.30 trillion budget for FY2025/26 — up from KES 3.99 trillion in FY2024/25. Revenue is projected at KES 3,368.6 billion, leaving a KES 933.3 billion deficit (4.6% of GDP). Education leads at KES 628.6 billion; debt interest at KES 1,007.4 billion remains a significant portion of expenditure.

citizen_impact.title: What this budget means for citizens
citizen_impact.source_note: Cited from seed budget_fy2025_26.json highlights & systemic_risks — no new figures.

blurbs.title: Debt service remains high
blurbs.text: Interest on public debt (KES 1,007.4B) accounts for nearly a quarter of the total budget — limiting fiscal space for development.

blurbs.title: Education leads again
blurbs.text: Education at KES 628.6B remains the largest sector allocation — about 14.6% of the total budget.

blurbs.title: County allocation up
blurbs.text: Parliament approved KES 415B equitable share to counties — up from KES 398B in FY2024/25.

2026/27.theme: Sustaining the Bottom-Up Economic Transformation Agenda (BETA) for Resilient and Inclusive Growth amid Global Uncertainty
2026/27.synopsis: Parliament approved a KES 4.82 trillion budget for FY2026/27 — up from KES 4,301.9 billion in FY2025/26. Revenue is projected at KES 3,630.5 billion, leaving a KES 1,146.2 billion deficit (5.5% of GDP). Education leads at KES 784.5 billion; debt interest at KES 1,203.1 billion exceeds total development spending of KES 750 billion.

citizen_impact.title: What this budget means for citizens
citizen_impact.source_note: Cited from seed budget_fy2026_27.json callouts & highlights — no new figures.

blurbs.title: Per citizen
blurbs.text: KES 4.82 trillion is approximately KES 96,400 per Kenyan (based on ~50M population).

blurbs.title: Debt exceeds development
blurbs.text: Debt interest (KES 1,203.1B) exceeds total development spending (KES 750B) for the first time at this scale.

blurbs.title: Education leads
blurbs.text: Education at KES 784.5B is the largest sector — about 16.3% of the total budget.

blurbs.title: County share approved higher
blurbs.text: Parliament approved KES 428B equitable share — up from KES 415B in FY2025/26 and the BPS proposal of KES 420B.
